evals.prompt: I have an OpenAPI spec at `evals/fixtures/openapi.yaml` and a pact file at `evals/fixtures/consumer-provider.json`. Which operations and status codes are not covered by my pact tests?
evals.expected_output: The agent runs parse_pact_coverage.py against the spec and pact file, then reports which operations, status codes, request body fields, and response body fields are missing coverage.

assertions.name: runs_coverage_script
assertions.description: Response invokes parse_pact_coverage.py rather than manually reasoning
assertions.value: The response invokes the parse_pact_coverage.py script (via uv run or equivalent) rather than attempting to manually compute coverage by reading the files

assertions.name: reports_missing_status_codes
assertions.description: Response identifies specific missing status codes
assertions.value: The response identifies specific status codes (such as 401 or 404) that are documented in the spec but missing from the pact interactions

assertions.name: reports_missing_resp_fields
assertions.description: Response reports missing required response body fields
assertions.value: The response identifies at least one required response body field that is documented in the spec but absent from the pact interaction response body

assertions.name: actionable_next_steps
assertions.description: Response suggests concrete steps to fill the gaps
assertions.value: The response gives concrete next steps to address the coverage gaps, such as adding pact interactions, enriching request/response bodies, or invoking the pact-generator agent

evals.prompt: My team says we have good pact coverage but I want to check. I have pacts in `pacts/` and my spec is `api.yaml`. Check all four coverage dimensions and tell me exactly what's missing, if anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the script across all four dimensions, lists specific missing items (not just percentages), and interprets the exit code.

assertions.name: covers_all_four_dimensions
assertions.description: Response addresses all four coverage dimensions
assertions.value: The response explicitly addresses all four coverage dimensions: (1) path/method coverage, (2) status code coverage, (3) required request body fields, (4) required response body fields — not just one or two

assertions.name: uses_glob_for_pacts_dir
assertions.description: Response uses a glob pattern for the pacts directory
assertions.value: The response passes a glob pattern like 'pacts/*.json' to --pacts rather than guessing a single filename

assertions.name: reports_specific_missing_items
assertions.description: Response lists specific NOT COVERED items, not just percentages
assertions.value: When gaps exist, the response lists the specific operations, status codes, or fields that are missing — it does not only report a coverage percentage

assertions.name: interprets_exit_code
assertions.description: Response interprets the script exit code
assertions.value: The response interprets the exit code of the script (0 = full coverage, 1 = gaps) and explains what it means

evals.prompt: Hypothetically, suppose I have already run pact-coverage and the report shows these gaps: POST /payments is not covered at all, GET /payments/{id} is missing the 404 status code, and the 200 response for GET /payments/{id} is missing the `amount` required field. Based on these stated gaps, what pact interactions do I need to add or modify?
evals.expected_output: The agent gives concrete guidance for all three gaps: a POST /payments interaction, a GET 404 interaction, and enriching the GET 200 response body to include amount.

assertions.name: addresses_all_three_gaps
assertions.description: Response addresses all three identified gaps
assertions.value: The response gives concrete guidance for all three gaps: the missing POST /payments path, the missing 404 status code for GET /payments/{id}, and the missing amount field in the 200 response

assertions.name: post_interaction_guidance
assertions.description: Response explains what the POST /payments interaction needs
assertions.value: The response explains what the POST /payments pact interaction needs to include (at minimum a 2xx response to cover path/method and status code dimensions)

assertions.name: refers_to_pact_generator
assertions.description: Response mentions the pact-generator agent or pactflow skill
assertions.value: The response references the pact-generator agent or the pactflow skill as the tool to use for actually writing the new Pact test interactions

assertions.name: response_field_guidance
assertions.description: Response explains how to fix the missing amount response field
assertions.value: The response explains that the existing GET /payments/{id} 200 interaction needs to have the amount field added to its response body content
